title: I Let the Rowing-Club Erg Booking Catch the Captain Who Ghosted

parts.text: I booked erg 3 at 5:45 a.m. and the captain was already on it with no reservation. The booking app he mandated said: NO-SHOW AFTER FIVE MINUTES RELEASES THE ERG. CAPTAINS BOOK TOO. I was twenty-five, novice, holding a lock screen that said mine. Captain Holt said, "Captains warm the room." I pointed at the app. He rowed harder. "Warmth doesn't RSVP." I photographed the empty booking under his name, my lock, and the clock at 5:51. Then I used the app's release on his ghosted 5:30 and claimed 3. At 5:52 the coach asked why Holt's name was on a ghost-booking ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The coach can see Holt on erg 3 with a ghosted 5:30 against the app he mandated.

social.video_title: The captain ghosted his own erg booking — Part 1/2
social.description: 5:45 lock screen, a captain already rowing, and an app he mandated. I released his ghost. Would you have waited on the dock?

parts.text: Holt called it leadership until the app emailed the log. I printed the ticket, the mandate, and the photo. I rowed. Holt booked 6:00 like a novice and told the boathouse the app was always about optics. Optics is a word captains use when a ghost has a timestamp. Erg policy now has a second line: WARMTH RSVPS. I keep 5:45. Holt shows. The flywheel finally has a name that matches.

social.video_title: Warmth RSVPs for the erg — Part 2/2
social.description: Ghost ticket, a real 6:00 booking, and a second line in the app. Was leadership ever a stolen 5:45?
